text:
Aisha (Support): FYI customer on Dedicated reported their ingestion pipeline failing — structured output mode returning concatenated/partial JSON fragments that can't be parsed. They pasted the raw response, see below.

Sam (Eng): Can you paste the exact raw HTTP response (including x-request-id) and the model/route they hit? Also what concurrency?

Aisha (Support): x-request-id: rx-7a2b-ccf5
Model: redwood-chat-4b-v1, route: /v1/generate/json-mode, concurrent clients: ~12.
Raw body from customer (truncated):
```
{"conversation_id":"conv-91","user_id":"u-12","response":{"answer":"Here is my data","meta":{"session":"sess-a"}}}{"conversation_id":"conv-92","user_id":"u-13","response":{"answer":"Second reply","meta":{"session":"sess-b"}}}
```
Parser errors: JSON::ParserError: unexpected token at '}{' — their ingestion expects a single JSON object or array.

Oliver (SRE): That looks like two objects concatenated, not an array. Could be our streaming/batcher stitched two sessions into one TCP stream chunk. Any deploys to batcher/prefetcher in the last 24h?

deploy-bot: Deploy redwood/batcher 2026-03-16T18:42Z (commit 9f3a7c4) to env:dedicated-prod

Ingrid (ML): I ran a quick local repro with the same model + `structured_output=true` and concurrency 12 — got intermittent concat of objects when prefix cache is on and the prefix key normalization collapsed different conversation ids. Repro steps:
1) Start two clients hitting the same route with different conversation_id header.
2) Enable prefix_cache and structured_output in config.
3) Observe raw stream contains back-to-back JSON objects without separators.

Sam (Eng): Reproduced here too. Minimal curl to repro: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Conversation-Id: conv-REPRO" -d '{"prompt":"{\"json_mode\":true} "}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/json-mode -N &
# run multiple times in parallel
```
Broken piece we saw in logs: 
```
[batcher] assigned batch=482 gpu=pool-a session_key=prefix:chat:redwood-chat-4b
[stream] write: {"conversation_id":"conv-123","response":{"answer":"PartA"}}{"conversation_id":"conv-124","response":{"answer":"PartB"}}
```

Aisha (Support): Customer is blocking production ingestion, their billing is fine but they're hitting parse failures across several tenants (shared dedicated pool). They're asking for immediate mitigation.

Oliver (SRE): Quick mitigation options: 1) toggle `prefix_cache=false` for that customer's route; 2) disable structured_output mode as a last resort; 3) patch batcher to include conversation_id in the prefix cache key. I'll roll a config toggle now for the customer's account.

Sam (Eng): Root cause: cache key normalization omitted conversation/session id so different sessions could reuse cached KV prefix; when two sessions finish close together the stream assembler concatenates cached suffix with new output chunk as a single response. Fix is to include conversation_id+session_token in cache namespace and make the stream assembler insert a safe delimiter for JSON-mode outputs (or always wrap multi-objects in an array when streaming).

Ingrid (ML): I prepared a minimal patch: `cache_key = f"{model}:{route}:{conversation_id}:{session_token}"` + guard to ensure structured output streaming enforces one-root object. Unit tests added for concurrent prefix hits. Will open PR now.

Aisha (Support): Customer agreed to temporary toggle. I've applied `prefix_cache=false` on their dedicated route and asked them to retry. They reported ingestion success after toggle (so mitigation works).

Sam (Eng): Plan: ship hotfix PR (include session in cache key + streaming guard) to batcher, roll to dedicated-prod with canary on 10% of traffic, monitor for concat regressions. If canary clean, finish rollout.

Oliver (SRE): I'll keep the cluster in mitigation state until patch is verified. Also adding alert for "json-mode: concatenated_objects" to catch future occurrences.

deploy-bot: CI passed for PR #4128, deploying canary (10%) to dedicated-prod.

Aisha (Support): Customer updated support ticket — parser errors stopped after toggle. I'll mark customer notified and closing escalation once we confirm prod patch.

Sam (Eng): Follow-up action items: [Sam] finish PR + release notes, [Oliver] keep mitigation flag and alert for 48h, [Ingrid] run load test with concurrency matrix and add regression test.

Ingrid (ML): Added regression test to CI that runs 20 concurrent sessions with structured_output enabled; will fail the build if any concatenated objects are produced.

Aisha (Support): Thanks everyone — tracking in the support ticket. :white_check_mark:
